full_judgment: 26. It is settled principle of law that the lower appellate Court being final Court of fact will have to discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the findings of the trial Court. In case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate Court to reassess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent finding. In the present suit I find that the specific findings of the trial Court have not been reversed by the appellate Court exercising in its power under Order XLI. rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In this connection reference may be made to the decision reported in 8 BLC (AD) (2003) 77.
